sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: This dictionary uses the "Taiwanese Hokkien Romanization Scheme (Tailo)" announced by the Ministry of Education on October 14, 2006, as its romanization system. Foreign words in the dictionary text are treated as Taiwanese Hokkien entries and marked with their original (non-sandhi) tone.

sections.title: Common tones
paragraphs: Common tones are classified as Tone 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, and 8. In the initial classification of Chinese, tones were divided into four categories (level, rising, departing, and entering), each further subdivided into yin and yang. However, various dialects underwent different evolutionary processes. In modern standard Taiwanese Hokkien, the yang rising tone has evolved to become identical to the yang departing tone, resulting in a total of seven tones.

sections.title: Special tones
bullets: Some dialect variations have Tone 6, for example: "ǒ" (numeric: o6).
The first syllable of combined sounds and three-syllable sequences may have Tone 9, for example: "ő" (numeric: o9).
The light-tone mark "--" is placed between a stressed syllable and a light-tone syllable. For example: āu--ji̍t (back--day), tsáu--tshut-khì (run--exit).

sections.title: Tone sandhi
paragraphs: In phrases and sentences, tone sandhi occurs, where a character's tone changes when followed by another character. However, there are exceptions: when the phrase ends, when the following syllable is in a weak tone, or when the subject is emphasized, the original tone may be maintained even within a sentence.

Because tone sandhi varies depending on how phrases are segmented, and segmentation can be done in multiple ways, this dictionary marks all tones as original tones without indicating sandhi changes. However, light tones are marked with "--" as needed according to context.

sections.title: Words without a fixed tone
paragraphs: Particles, exclamations, and grammatical words without fixed tones are conventionally written with the Tone 4 glottal-stop ending "-h". Since these are typically read lightly and do not affect tone sandhi in the preceding character, the light-tone mark "--" is added according to the Taiwanese Hokkien Romanization Scheme.
